tldr: This thread is now a run of independent arXiv papers on diffusion language models, not one event or vendor launch. It opened Nov 3 with hallucination in multimodal dLLMs, moved to which tokens can be committed in parallel (Nov 5), then to block-diffusion inference cost and speculative drafting (Nov 6-10).
whats_new: Two Nov 19 papers attack the denoising step count directly: one calibrates the cheapest schedule per task, model and sampler instead of using one fixed schedule, and dLoop refines latents recurrently to commit more tokens per step.
why_it_matters: The open problem for diffusion LMs has shifted from "can they generate in parallel" to "how many denoising steps does a given workload really need", which is the number that sets their serving latency and cost.

beats.headline: Multimodal diffusion LMs inherit the hallucination problem
beats.summary: VIGOR orders mask predictions by visual gain to cut hallucinations in multimodal discrete diffusion LMs.

beats.headline: Which tokens can be committed together without changing the output
beats.summary: Two papers replace the independent-sampling shortcut: one measures token coupling directly, the other simulates the continuous-time chain exactly.

beats.headline: Block diffusion gets sparse attention, overlapping blocks and draft trees
beats.summary: Work targets repeated prefix attention, block-boundary latency, and block-diffusion drafters for speculative decoding of autoregressive models.

beats.headline: Fewer, better-chosen denoising steps: remasking, adaptive schedules, looped refinement
beats.summary: The latest papers decide when to revise a token and how many steps a workload needs, rather than speeding up each step.

open_questions: Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
Do task-calibrated denoising schedules keep quality on agentic and tool-calling workloads, not only the paper's benchmarks?
Do block-diffusion drafters like DForkTree beat standard autoregressive drafters on end-to-end tokens per second in a production speculative-decoding stack?
Does learned remasking transfer from Sudoku diagnostics to code and long-form text generation?
Is there a head-to-head latency and quality comparison of a diffusion LM against a same-size autoregressive model at matched serving cost?
take_for_builders: Do not plan capacity around diffusion LMs yet; if you evaluate one, record denoising steps per request and quality per task, because the schedule papers show the cheapest safe step count varies by workload.

day_captions.57b08f9866a26766: Starting point: a reliability problem, hallucination in multimodal discrete diffusion LMs, mitigated by ordering mask predictions by visual gain.
day_captions.0491c6de7a511fb5: Shifts to parallel decoding: measures how committing one token changes another instead of using a mean-field similarity proxy.
day_captions.2fb1a0f31494270f: Same question, exact answer: speculative simulation of the continuous-time Markov chain so parallel sampling keeps the output distribution.
day_captions.5fbc35eb022e4033: First block-diffusion cost paper: sparsifies both historical-prefix attention and current-block processing.
day_captions.0aacbce5f85ac122: Uses block diffusion as a drafter: fork-aware draft trees for speculative decoding of a target model.
day_captions.ca0cd6bcfdb70098: Overlaps denoising blocks so block diffusion LMs stop paying latency at block boundaries.
day_captions.679b2c4e802619e6: Turns to self-correction: hidden states expose errors that token confidence misses, so a learned signal decides when to remask.
day_captions.cbe67172baf08ac4: Shows the cheapest quality-preserving schedule depends on task, model and sampler, and calibrates it per workload.
day_captions.a8a16da3f476938c: Newest: recurrent latent refinement so more token predictions become reliable enough to commit at each step.
